2	title: "ProRes"
3	description: "Export a ProRes 422 or ProRes 4444 master for another application, and see what each one keeps."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	ProRes files are masters: their next reader is another application, not a viewer. ProRes 422 is the one to reach for first. ProRes 4444 is larger, and you choose it when you need the alpha channel.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  where="Export sheet ▸ Format"
12	  tools="export"
13	/>
14	
15	| | ProRes 422 (MOV) | ProRes 4444 (MOV) |
16	| --- | --- | --- |
17	| Picture | 10-bit | 12-bit |
18	| Keeps transparency | No | Yes |
19	| Odd width or height | Written one pixel smaller | Kept |
20	| A custom size of a different shape | Letterboxed with black | Won't export |
21	
22	Both are `.mov` files with these in common:
23	
24	- The data rate is fixed by the profile, so **Quality:** is greyed out.
25	- The sound is 16-bit, 48 kHz stereo LPCM. **Bit depth:** is greyed out, because 24-bit is for WAV and AIFF.
26	- Both can carry HDR. In an HLG project they write HLG unless you change **Dynamic Range:**. See [Export HDR](/hdr/export-hdr/).
27	- [Chapters](/export/chapters/) are written.
28	- [Fast start](/export/h264-and-hevc/#fast-start) is off, because an editing master has no need of it.
29	
30	## ProRes 422 (MOV)
31	
32	Use this as an editing master for another application. It keeps 10 bits of Frame Job's deep frames.
33	
34	ProRes 422 has no alpha channel, so a transparent canvas is flattened onto black.
35	
36	## ProRes 4444 (MOV)
37	
38	Use this for a title, a lower third or anything else another application will composite over its own footage. It keeps 12 bits and the alpha channel, and the [footnote](/export/export-sheet/#the-footnote) ends in `alpha`. The colour is straight, not multiplied by the transparency, so a re-imported file composites to the right colour.
39	
40	It's the only movie format that keeps an odd width or height.
41	
42	A **Custom…** size of a different shape from the canvas won't export, because padding would lose the alpha. After the save panel the export stops with a message naming the canvas's size. Every row in the **Size:** popup has the canvas's shape, and any custom size in the same proportions is fine.

1	---
2	title: "AV1 and VP9"
3	description: "Export small delivery files and web movies with Frame Job's built-in AV1 and VP9 encoders, and know how their rates, time and memory behave."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	AV1 and VP9 are the formats for the smallest delivery files and for the web. Frame Job has their encoders built in, SVT-AV1 and libvpx, and they run in software, so they take longer than HEVC.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  where={['Export sheet ▸ Format', 'Export sheet ▸ Speed (AV1 only)']}
12	  tools="export"
13	/>
14	
15	| Format | File | Sound | Picture | Keeps transparency | Can carry HDR | **Speed:** |
16	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
17	| [AV1 (MP4)](#av1-mp4) | `.mp4` | AAC | 10-bit | No | Yes | Yes |
18	| [AV1 (WebM)](#av1-webm) | `.webm` | Opus | 10-bit | No | Yes | Yes |
19	| [VP9 (WebM)](#vp9-webm) | `.webm` | Opus | 8-bit, or 10-bit with HDR | No | Yes | Greyed out |
20	| [VP9 with Alpha (WebM)](#vp9-with-alpha-webm) | `.webm` | Opus | 8-bit | Yes | No | Greyed out |
21	
22	All four write a keyframe at least every 2 seconds and need even dimensions, so an odd width or height is written one pixel smaller. All four write [chapters](/export/chapters/). The sheet [estimates the time](/export/export-sheet/#estimated-time) before you start.
23	
24	## AV1 (MP4)
25	
26	This is the smallest delivery file: AV1 video and AAC sound in an MP4. It's always 10-bit.
27	
28	**Speed:** offers **Faster**, **Balanced** and **Smaller file**, with **Balanced** the default. See [Encoder speed](/export/encoder-speed/). Slower settings take longer and write a smaller file.
29	
30	It encodes at a constant quality matched to HEVC, with the rate as a [soft cap](#the-rate-as-a-soft-cap). It's one of the six formats that can carry HDR. See [Export HDR](/hdr/export-hdr/).
31	
32	An M1 or M2 Mac can't [play the file back](#playback-on-m1-and-m2-macs).
33	
34	## AV1 (WebM)
35	
36	The same AV1 picture in a WebM file, for the web. It has the same encoder, speeds, soft cap and HDR as AV1 (MP4). Only the container and the sound differ.
37	
38	The sound is Opus, 48 kHz stereo, at 192 kbps unless a [Quality tier](/export/quality/) says otherwise, and it snaps to the nearest rate the encoder offers. A project with no sound exports a WebM with no sound track.
39	
40	## VP9 (WebM)
41	
42	VP9 in a WebM file with Opus sound: the web format every browser plays. It's larger than AV1 for the same picture and slower to export than HEVC. It has one speed, so **Speed:** is greyed out.
43	
44	An SDR picture is 8-bit, in VP9's Profile 0, which every player decodes. HDR is 10-bit, in Profile 2. VP9 can't name HLG or PQ itself, so the WebM file tells the player which one it is. See [Export HDR](/hdr/export-hdr/).
45	
46	## VP9 with Alpha (WebM)
47	
48	VP9 (WebM) that keeps a transparent canvas, for a title or lower third a web page plays over its own background in Chrome or Firefox. Safari hasn't been confirmed to show its transparency, and Safari's transparent movie is [HEVC with Alpha (MOV)](/export/h264-and-hevc/#hevc-with-alpha-mov). Only a player that decodes VP9 with libvpx shows the transparency, and others show the picture opaque.
49	
50	- The picture is 8-bit, with the transparency as a second stream beside it. The [footnote](/export/export-sheet/#the-footnote) ends in `alpha`.
51	- It's SDR only, so an HDR project writes its SDR version, and **Dynamic Range:** stays greyed out on **SDR version**.
52	- The sound is Opus, as in VP9 (WebM).
53	- A **Custom…** size of a different shape from the canvas won't export, because padding would lose the alpha. After the save panel the export stops with a message naming the canvas's size. Every row in the **Size:** popup is fine.
54	- Imported back into Frame Job it shows opaque, with black where it was transparent. For a transparent clip to bring back in, export ProRes 4444 or HEVC with Alpha.
55	
56	## The rate as a soft cap
57	
58	On AV1 and VP9 the video rate isn't a target. They encode at a constant quality chosen to match or beat HEVC at that rate, and the file usually stays under it. That's why the Quality tiers and the footnote read `usually ≤ …`.
59	
60	- With **Format default** the cap is HEVC's rate. With a tier it's 60 % of the H.264 rate, as for HEVC. See [Export quality](/export/quality/).
61	- Simple footage comes out much smaller than the rate.
62	- Very detailed footage can go over it: up to about 1.25 times on AV1, and about 1.15 times on VP9.
63	- In an HDR export, VP9 matches HEVC 10-bit at that rate.
64	- You can't know the file size in advance.
65	
66	On VP9 with Alpha the rate is the picture's alone. The transparency is a second stream at a fixed quality on top of it, so the file is larger than the rate says. On a moving soft-edged shape, the transparency measured about 6 to 15 % of the video at 1080p, 9 to 21 % at 720p, and 21 to 39 % at 640 × 360, with the higher figures at the Low tier.
67	
68	## Memory and the queue
69	
70	A job in the [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/) waits while the AV1 and VP9 exports already running would use more than a quarter of the Mac's memory with it. Its row says why, for example "Waiting for memory: AV1 and VP9 exports running now hold about 6.0 GB of the 8.0 GB this Mac allows them, and this one needs about 3.0 GB." A later job may run first meanwhile.
71	
72	A job always starts when no other AV1 or VP9 export is running. **Export…** never waits, so starting several at once behind their progress sheets can go past that quarter. The memory each job needs is a measured figure, not a guarantee, and a heavier timeline can use more.
73	
74	## Playback on M1 and M2 Macs
75	
76	M1 and M2 Macs have no AV1 decoder, so neither Frame Job nor QuickTime can play or re-import an AV1 file there, MP4 or WebM. The Mac can still export one.
77	
78	A VP9 (WebM) file re-imports on any Apple silicon Mac.
79	
80	## Good to know
81	
82	An AV1 rate is held at 100 Mbps at most.
83

8	
9	GIF and APNG are for short silent loops you can send or drop into a page. Each stores every frame as a whole picture, so a long or large one quickly becomes a file nobody can send. That's why both start small and hold at most 600 frames.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  where="Export sheet ▸ Format"
13	  tools="export"
14	/>
15	
16	## Export a loop
17	
18	<Steps>
19	
20	1. Set an [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) around the moment you want.
21	
22	2. Press <kbd>⌘E</kbd>, and choose **Animated GIF** or **Animated PNG** from **Format:**.
23	
24	3. Set **Range:** to **In/out range**.
25	
26	4. Check the readout, which shows the size and the frame count, such as `· 360 frames, no audio`.
27	
28	5. Choose **Export…**.
29	
30	</Steps>
31	
32	## Animated GIF
33	
34	A GIF is a short, silent `.gif` that loops forever. It starts at 480 × 270 and 12.5 fps, and you can still change the size and the rate.
35	
36	The 12.5 is deliberate. A GIF stores each frame's delay in hundredths of a second, so only rates that divide 100 play back exactly. 25 and 50 fps from the **Frame rate:** popup do too, and any other rate lands wherever the format's rounding puts it.
37	
38	A GIF has a palette of 256 colours. It can show a pixel as fully transparent but has no partial transparency, so soft edges go hard, and it isn't one of the [formats that keep transparency](/export/transparency/).
39	
40	## Animated PNG
41	
42	An APNG is a lossless, silent, true-colour `.png` that loops forever. It starts at 960 × 540 and 25 fps, and you can still change the size and the rate.
43	
44	It keeps real transparency, so a pixel can be any fraction of opaque, and the [footnote](/export/export-sheet/#the-footnote) ends in `alpha`. It's written at 8 bits a component and labelled BT.709.
45	
46	A viewer that knows nothing of APNG shows the first frame.
47	
48	## The 600-frame limit
49	
50	An animated GIF or APNG holds at most 600 frames. That's 48 seconds at GIF's 12.5 fps, or 24 seconds at APNG's 25 fps. The readout shows the count while you're choosing, but the sheet doesn't stop you. Once you've picked where to save, a longer export stops before it writes anything:
51	
52	> An animated GIF is limited to 600 frames and this range is 720. Shorten the range, or lower the export frame rate.
53	
54	For GIF the way out is a shorter range, because every fixed rate in the **Frame rate:** popup is higher than 12.5 fps. An APNG can go down to 24 or 23.976 fps, which gains you about a second.
55	
56	## Fitting inside the size
57	
58	The **Size:** popup lists **GIF default** or **APNG default** first, and it's the default for those two formats and no others. Each is 480 × 270 or 960 × 540, fitted to the canvas's shape.
59	
60	Every row, and a **Custom…** size, is a box the picture fits inside. It keeps its shape and is never enlarged, and nothing is letterboxed. The rows show the size the file will have. A 1080 × 1920 project's GIF default is 152 × 270.
61	
62	Because the picture is never enlarged, rows bigger than the canvas come out as the canvas's own size, and the popup hides rows that repeat an earlier row's numbers. An odd width or height is kept.
63	
64	## Good to know
65	
66	- **Quality:** and **Loudness:** are greyed out, and so are **Bit depth:** and **Stems:**. Neither format has a bit rate or any sound.
67	- **Burn in timecode** still works.
68	- Neither format has [chapters](/export/chapters/).
69	- Both write the SDR version in an HDR project.

3	/// The export sheet's ANSWER half: read the controls, ask the core what they
4	/// describe, and repaint the card from what it said.
5	///
6	/// The seam is the §7 rule the sheet is built on, drawn as a file boundary.
7	/// `ExportSheetController.swift` owns the controls — it makes the popups and
8	/// the fields, lists the sizes, and hands a person something to choose with.
9	/// Nothing there decides an output size, a rate or a duration, because
10	/// nothing in this dialog does: every number the card shows comes back from
11	/// `rc_export_settings`, and this file is the whole of the round trip. It
12	/// turns a selection into the override object the core reads (`overrides()`),
13	/// sends it (`resolve()`), and writes the answer into the readout, the
14	/// footnote and the controls' enablement (`syncReadout()`). Between those
15	/// three, the `current…` accessors are the one place a popup index becomes a
16	/// meaning, so a control's index arithmetic is never spelled twice.
17	///
18	/// The one number the sheet DOES choose is the bit rate, and it is here for
19	/// that reason rather than beside the Quality popup: a tier is a REQUEST
20	/// (`ExportSheetOptions.swift` holds the ladder), and turning one into bits
21	/// per second needs the frame the controls are asking for — which is
22	/// `requestedFormat()`, three accessors deep into this file and nowhere near
23	/// the popup.
24	///
25	/// The cut is the size payment `ExportSheetController.swift` owed at 1114
26	/// lines against app/CLAUDE.md's ~600 cap, and it is a pure move: the same
27	/// methods, in the same order, with the same bodies. **The toll is
28	/// visibility**, for the reason `ExporterLoudness.swift` records — `private`
29	/// on an extension member reaches only its own file, and a stored property
30	/// cannot live in an extension at all. So every control, every field and
31	/// every piece of state this file reads is internal in the file that
32	/// declares it, and the four members the controls call back into —
33	/// `resolve()`, `currentPreset`, `isCustomSize` and `isCustomLoudness` — are
34	/// internal here. Everything else below stays `private`, because a `private`
35	/// extension member is reachable from the rest of THIS file, and nothing
36	/// outside it has ever asked.
37	/// Phase 7 added the OTHER direction to this file, and it belongs here for the
38	/// same reason the first one does: `currentChoice` is a reading of the
39	/// controls, exactly as `overrides()` is, and `apply(_:)` is that reading run
40	/// backwards. Keeping the pair together is what makes a saved preset and the
41	/// remembered choice provably the same thing as clicking each control by hand —
42	/// there is one account of what a stored choice means, and both halves of it
43	/// are on one screen.

48	    /// Asks the core for the settings the current controls describe, then
49	    /// repaints the readout from the answer.
50	    ///
51	    /// A refusal is not an error dialog: the message goes in the readout and
52	    /// Export greys out, so a bad override reads as "this combination is not
53	    /// available" rather than interrupting the person adjusting it.
54	    func resolve() {
55	        guard let project = editor?.document?.project, let preset = currentPreset else {
56	            resolved = nil
57	            resolveError = "This build has no export presets."
58	            syncReadout()
59	            return
60	        }
61	        // A format whose sizes the core could not list is not exported at
62	        // all, whatever the settings call would answer: the one refusal
63	        // `rc_export_sizes` shares with `rc_export_settings` is an unknown
64	        // preset, but a listing can also fail on its own (a reply this
65	        // build cannot decode), and the size the sheet would then send is
66	        // the fields' clamped floor, 16 × 16, which nobody asked for.
67	        if let message = sizesError {
68	            resolved = nil
69	            resolveError = message
70	            syncReadout()
71	            return
72	        }
73	        // An empty Custom field is not a size. Its formatter accepts the
74	        // empty string as "no value", `integerValue` reads that as 0, and
75	        // the clamp would turn it into the 16-pixel floor — an export
76	        // nobody asked for, reached by clearing a field and clicking
77	        // Export…, since that click commits the field before it reads.
78	        if isCustomSize, currentApplies.size,
79	            widthField.stringValue.isEmpty || heightField.stringValue.isEmpty
80	        {
81	            resolved = nil
82	            resolveError = "Type a width and a height, or pick a size from the list."
83	            syncReadout()
84	            return
85	        }
86	        // The same rule for the Custom loudness field, and for the same
87	        // reason: an empty field is not a target, and reading it as one would
88	        // export at whatever the clamp's floor happens to be.
89	        if isCustomLoudness, currentApplies.loudness, loudnessField.stringValue.isEmpty {
90	            resolved = nil
91	            resolveError = "Type a loudness target in LUFS, or pick one from the list."
92	            syncReadout()
93	            return
94	        }
95	        do {
96	            resolved = try ReelExport.settings(
97	                project, preset: preset.id, overrides: overrides())
98	            resolveError = nil
99	        } catch {
100	            resolved = nil
101	            resolveError = error.localizedDescription
102	        }
103	        syncReadout()
104	    }

108	    /// The controls as an `ExportChoice`, with the sheet's own gating applied:
109	    /// a control the chosen format cannot take (`Applies`) contributes
110	    /// nothing, exactly as it contributes no override. So a preset saved off

282	    /// True while the Loudness popup's last item, "Custom…", is chosen.

288	    /// the popup, on the Quality row's established rule that the first item
289	    /// is no override at all. Nil too for a format with no sound, so a target

291	    private var currentLoudness: Double? {
292	        guard currentApplies.loudness else { return nil }
293	        let index = loudnessPopup.indexOfSelectedItem
294	        if index >= 1, index <= Self.loudnessTargets.count {
295	            return Self.loudnessTargets[index - 1]
296	        }
297	        guard isCustomLoudness, !loudnessField.stringValue.isEmpty else { return nil }
298	        let value = loudnessField.doubleValue
299	        guard value.isFinite else { return nil }

301	            max(value, Self.loudnessRange.lowerBound), Self.loudnessRange.upperBound)

304	    /// The size override, or nil when the Size popup is on its first row.
305	    ///
306	    /// That row is the format's default — the first of the core's list and
307	    /// of `visibleSizes` alike, since nothing precedes it to hide it — and
308	    /// it is sent as NO override rather than as its own numbers so that
309	    /// what ⌘E exports and what the `export` tool exports with no `size`
310	    /// are one code path in the core — the default lives in
311	    /// `export_size.rs`, not in two readings of it. Any other row sends
312	    /// that row's numbers; "Custom…" sends the fields', clamped. Nil too
313	    /// for a format that has no frames, so a size picked for a movie cannot
314	    /// follow the user into an audio-only export.
315	    private func sizeOverride() -> (width: Int, height: Int)? {
316	        guard currentApplies.size else { return nil }
317	        if isCustomSize {
318	            return (clampedSize(widthField), clampedSize(heightField))
319	        }
320	        let index = sizePopup.indexOfSelectedItem
321	        guard index > 0, index < visibleSizes.count else { return nil }
322	        return (visibleSizes[index].width, visibleSizes[index].height)
323	    }

325	    /// The frame the controls are ASKING for: the same numbers `overrides()`
326	    /// sends, plus the fallbacks the core would apply to them.
327	    ///
328	    /// The tiers are computed against this rather than against `resolved`,
329	    /// which still describes the PREVIOUS format at the moment a new one is
330	    /// being resolved — the bit rate would then be one change behind the
331	    /// size it was supposed to be for.
332	    private func requestedFormat() -> (width: Int, height: Int, fps: Fps) {
333	        let canvas = editor?.document?.project.snapshot.canvas ?? CanvasSnapshot()
334	        // No override resolves to the Size popup's first row. The format's
335	        // own cap, then the canvas, stand in for it only when the listing
336	        // failed — the same fallback the core applies to a preset with no
337	        // size (`export.rs`).
338	        var width = sizes.first?.width ?? currentPreset?.width ?? canvas.width
339	        var height = sizes.first?.height ?? currentPreset?.height ?? canvas.height
340	        if let size = sizeOverride() {
341	            width = size.width
342	            height = size.height
343	        }
344	        return (width, height, currentRate ?? canvas.fps)
345	    }

347	    /// The override object, with every key the controls are NOT overriding
348	    /// left out — the same rule the op builders follow, so the core's own
349	    /// defaults apply (§6). Keys are the core's override names in
350	    /// `export.rs` — `width`, `height`, `fps`, `range`, `video_bitrate`,
351	    /// `audio_bitrate`.
352	    private func overrides() -> [String: Any]? {
353	        var overrides: [String: Any] = [:]
354	        let applies = currentApplies
355	        let format = requestedFormat()
356	        if let size = sizeOverride() {
357	            overrides["width"] = size.width
358	            overrides["height"] = size.height
359	        }
360	        if let fps = currentRate {
361	            overrides["fps"] = [fps.num, fps.den]
362	        }
363	        // Bits per second: the unit `export.rs` reads these two overrides in,
364	        // and the one `AVVideoAverageBitRateKey` takes after it. They are
365	        // sent separately because a preset may take one and not the other —
366	        // the audio-only row has no video rate to set, and a frame-sequence
367	        // row has neither.
368	        if let tier = currentTier {
369	            if applies.videoBitrate {
370	                overrides["video_bitrate"] = tier.videoBitsPerSecond(
371	                    width: format.width, height: format.height, fps: format.fps,
372	                    codec: currentPreset?.codec ?? "")
373	            }
374	            if applies.audioBitrate {
375	                overrides["audio_bitrate"] = tier.audioBitsPerSecond
376	            }
377	        }
378	        // Both loudness keys together: the ceiling, fixed at −1 dBTP and
379	        // named in the hint, is the master limiter's (spec §11 AU-27), which
380	        // holds −1 unsent too, so a ceiling goes only beside a target.
381	        if let target = currentLoudness {
382	            overrides["loudness_lufs"] = target
383	            overrides["peak_dbtp"] = Self.peakCeilingDBTP
384	        }
385	        // The core reads the range as ONE nested object (`export.rs`), and
386	        // ignores override keys it does not know — so `start` and `duration`
387	        // spelled at the top level exported the whole project instead of the
388	        // in/out range, silently.
389	        if let picture = dynamicRangeOverride() { overrides["dynamic_range"] = picture }
390	        if let speed = encoderSpeedOverride() { overrides["encoder_speed"] = speed }
391	        if let bits = audioBitsOverride() { overrides["audio_bits"] = bits }
392	        if let stems = stemsOverride() { overrides["stems"] = stems }
393	        if rangePopup.indexOfSelectedItem == 1, let range = range {
394	            overrides["range"] = [
395	                "start": range.start,
396	                "duration": max(0, range.end - range.start),
397	            ]
398	        }
399	        return overrides.isEmpty ? nil : overrides
400	    }

402	    private func clampedSize(_ field: NSTextField) -> Int {

406	    /// Rewrites the readout, the footnote, the controls' enablement and the
407	    /// Export button from `resolved`. The size fields follow the core while
408	    /// a row of the Size popup owns the size, which is what makes "Custom…"
409	    /// readable: pick it and the fields already hold the numbers to edit.

411	    /// Enablement comes from the FORMAT rather than from `resolved`, so a
412	    /// refused resolve leaves the controls where they were instead of
413	    /// greying out the very one that has to be changed to fix it.
414	    private func syncReadout() {
415	        let applies = currentApplies
416	        let custom = isCustomSize
417	        // A popup whose listing failed holds nothing to choose, and the one
418	        // control that can put a size back is the Format popup, so the size
419	        // controls grey out with it — the exception to the rule in the doc
420	        // comment above, for the one refusal no size can fix.
421	        let listed = sizesError == nil
422	        sizePopup.isEnabled = applies.size && listed
423	        for field in [widthField, heightField] {
424	            field.isEnabled = applies.size && listed && custom
425	            field.textColor = field.isEnabled ? DS.textStrong : DS.textMuted
426	        }
427	        ratePopup.isEnabled = applies.frameRate
428	        qualityPopup.isEnabled = applies.quality
429	        syncQualityTitles(applies)
430	        loudnessPopup.isEnabled = applies.loudness
431	        loudnessField.isEnabled = applies.loudness && isCustomLoudness
432	        loudnessField.textColor = loudnessField.isEnabled ? DS.textStrong : DS.textMuted
433	        if !isCustomLoudness {
434	            // The field mirrors the row that is chosen, exactly as the size
435	            // fields mirror the core's answer, so picking "Custom…" starts
436	            // from the number that was in force a moment before. "Off" has no
437	            // number of its own, so it shows the first target — the one
438	            // Custom is most likely to be an adjustment of.
439	            loudnessField.doubleValue = currentLoudness ?? Self.loudnessTargets[0]
440	        }
441	        // The last control on the card, and the last one to be gated: the
442	        // burn-in stayed live on the three audio-only rows, alone among the
443	        // format-dependent controls, offering to write a timecode into a file
444	        // with no picture to write it into.
445	        burnInCheckbox.isEnabled = applies.burnIn
446	        syncDynamicRange(applies)
447	        syncSpeed(applies)
448	        syncAudioBits(applies)
449	        syncStems(applies)
450	
451	        guard let settings = resolved else {
452	            summaryLabel.stringValue = resolveError ?? "These settings are not available."
453	            summaryLabel.textColor = DS.textStrong
454	            footnote.stringValue = ""
455	            footnote.toolTip = nil
456	            exportButton?.isEnabled = false
457	            return
458	        }
459	        if !custom {
460	            widthField.integerValue = settings.width
461	            heightField.integerValue = settings.height
462	        }
463	        summaryLabel.textColor = DS.textMuted
464	        summaryLabel.stringValue = summary(for: settings)
465	        footnote.stringValue = footnoteText(for: settings)
466	        footnote.toolTip = footnote.stringValue
467	        exportButton?.isEnabled = settings.duration > 0
468	    }

470	    /// Re-titles the tier rows with the rate each would ask for at the size
471	    /// and frame rate now chosen. "High" on its own says nothing; "High ·
472	    /// 8.0 Mbps" is the control's actual promise, and it has to move when
473	    /// the frame it is a rate for moves.
474	    private func syncQualityTitles(_ applies: Applies) {
475	        let format = requestedFormat()
476	        let codec = currentPreset?.codec ?? ""
477	        for (index, tier) in Self.tiers.enumerated() {
478	            guard let item = qualityPopup.item(at: index + 1) else { continue }
479	            if applies.videoBitrate {
480	                let rate = tier.videoBitsPerSecond(
481	                    width: format.width, height: format.height, fps: format.fps, codec: codec)
482	                let soft = applies.softCap ? "usually ≤ " : ""   // spec §11 CX-13
483	                item.title = "\(tier.name) · \(soft)\(Self.rateText(rate))"
484	            } else if applies.audioBitrate {
485	                item.title = "\(tier.name) · \(Self.rateText(tier.audioBitsPerSecond))"
486	            } else {
487	                item.title = tier.name
488	            }
489	        }
490	    }

492	    /// The one-line description of what the file will contain.
493	    private func summary(for settings: ExportSettings) -> String {
494	        if settings.isAudioOnly {
495	            // Milliseconds rather than frames, and no rate in the line: audio
496	            // has no frames, which is the same reason the rate popup is
497	            // greyed out for this preset.
498	            let duration = ReelTime.format(settings.duration, fps: settings.fps, frames: false)
499	            return "Audio only · \(duration)"
500	        }
501	        let duration = ReelTime.format(settings.duration, fps: settings.fps, frames: true)
502	        var text = "\(settings.width) × \(settings.height) · \(settings.fps.displayName) fps · "
503	            + duration
504	        if Self.isFrameSequence(container: settings.container) {
505	            // What a GIF or an APNG costs is frames, not seconds — and it
506	            // carries no audio however much of it the timeline has, which is
507	            // worth saying before the export rather than after it.
508	            text += " · \(settings.sequenceFrameCount ?? 0) frames, no audio"
509	        }
510	        // A bundled encoder's estimate (spec §11 CX-18 (9)).
511	        if let line = ExportEncoderCosts.sheetLine(for: settings) { text += "\n" + line }
512	        return text
513	    }

515	    /// The footnote over the buttons: the codec, the container, and the rates
516	    /// the CORE resolved — never the ones the tier asked for, and not filtered by
517	    /// what the sheet thinks applies, since a preset is free to carry a rate
518	    /// of its own that no control here offered.
519	    ///
520	    /// The distinction matters because `export.rs` drops override keys it
521	    /// does not know, silently (the same trap the range comment above names).
522	    /// A tier picked against a core that has no bit-rate overrides has to
523	    /// read as "the format's own rate" rather than let the popup imply a
524	    /// number the file will not have.
525	    private func footnoteText(for settings: ExportSettings) -> String {
526	        var parts = [settings.codec.uppercased()]
527	        let container = settings.container.uppercased()
528	        // A frame-sequence preset's codec IS its container: "GIF · GIF".
529	        if container != parts[0] { parts.append(container) }
530	        if let speed = settings.encoderSpeed { parts.append(speed.menuName) }
531	        if settings.audioBits == 24 { parts.append("24-bit") }
532	        if case let n = settings.stems.count, n > 0 { parts.append(n == 1 ? "1 stem" : "\(n) stems") }
533	        if let rate = settings.videoBitrate {
534	            // A bundled encoder's rate is a soft cap (spec §11 CX-13).
535	            parts.append((settings.writer == nil ? "" : "usually ≤ ") + Self.rateText(rate))
536	        }
537	        if let rate = settings.audioBitrate {
538	            parts.append("\(Self.rateText(rate)) audio")
539	        }
540	        if currentTier != nil, settings.videoBitrate == nil, settings.audioBitrate == nil {
541	            parts.append("format's own rate")
542	        }
543	        // The core's echo, not the popup's row: a build whose
544	        // `export_settings` has never heard of `loudness_lufs` drops the key
545	        // silently, and the footnote must not then promise a normalisation
546	        // the file will not have.
547	        if let target = settings.loudnessLufs {
548	            parts.append(
549	                String(format: "%g LUFS", target).replacingOccurrences(of: "-", with: "−"))
550	        }
551	        // Whether the ENCODING carries a fourth channel — the core's own
552	        // answer for this row (`ExportSettings.alpha`), never a reading of the
553	        // canvas. It is the one place the sheet says which format keeps a
554	        // transparent background, and it is a POSITIVE claim only: the rows
555	        // that answer false are not enumerated here, because the flag says
556	        // what the settings object says and the footnote's whole rule is that
557	        // it reports the core rather than the popup.
558	        if settings.alpha { parts.append("alpha") }
559	        return parts.joined(separator: " · ")
560	    }
561	}

3	/// What the export sheet's controls MEAN, before any of them has been read:
4	/// the ranges the fields accept, the loudness targets and the fixed ceiling,
5	/// the quality ladder and its arithmetic, and `Applies` — the one reading of
6	/// a format that decides which of the sheet's controls that row can honestly
7	/// take.
8	///
9	/// The seam is between a control's VOCABULARY and its VALUE.
10	/// `ExportSheetController.swift` builds the popups and the fields and puts
11	/// the card up; `ExportSheetResolve.swift` reads what is chosen and asks the
12	/// core about it. Everything here is what both of them consult and neither
13	/// of them owns: it depends on no popup's selection, holds no state, and
14	/// would answer the same for a sheet that was never shown. That is also why
15	/// the two nested types live in this half rather than beside the controls
16	/// they gate — `QualityTier` is a bit-rate calculation and `Applies` is a
17	/// reading of one `ExportPreset` row, and neither has ever asked an
18	/// `NSPopUpButton` a question.
19	///
20	/// The cut is the size payment `ExportSheetController.swift` owed at 1114
21	/// lines against app/CLAUDE.md's ~600 cap, and it is a pure move: the same
22	/// declarations, in the same order, with the same bodies. **The toll is
23	/// visibility.** `private` on an extension member reaches only its own file,
24	/// so `loudnessTargets`, `loudnessRange`, `tiers`, `QualityTier`, `Applies`,
25	/// `isFrameSequence` and `rateText` are all internal now, for the reason
26	/// `ExporterLoudness.swift` records: the split, and nothing else. `sizeRange`
27	/// and `peakCeilingDBTP` were already internal and say in their own comments
28	/// why. `loudnessTitle` arrived later, in phase 7, and for the other reason a
29	/// member moves: the controller was at the cap and had to give something up
30	/// before it took the Preset row on.
31	extension ExportSheetController {
32	
33	    /// The widest and narrowest custom size the fields accept. Not a format
34	    /// limit: a sanity range so a mistyped digit cannot ask the encoder for a
35	    /// 300 000-pixel frame.
36	    /// Internal, not private: the agent's `export` refuses a custom size
37	    /// outside it by name (`AgentServer+Export.swift`), and one constant is
38	    /// how the sheet and the tool cannot disagree.
39	    static let sizeRange = 16...8192
40	
41	    // MARK: - Loudness
42	
43	    /// The Loudness popup's rows after "Off", in menu order: the integrated
44	    /// target each asks the export to be normalised to.
45	    ///
46	    /// −14 LUFS is where every streaming service has settled (Spotify,
47	    /// YouTube and Apple Music all normalise to within a decibel of it), −16
48	    /// is the podcast convention for stereo, and −23 is EBU R 128, which is
49	    /// broadcast delivery in Europe and what "LUFS" meant before streaming
50	    /// took the word. Anything else is "Custom…" and the field beside it.
51	    static let loudnessTargets: [Double] = [-14, -16, -23]
52	
53	    /// The true-peak ceiling of the master limiter every export with sound
54	    /// runs (spec §11 AU-27), in dBTP, sent only beside a loudness target —
55	    /// unsent, the master holds the same −1 (`ExportLoudness.defaultCeiling`).
56	    /// FIXED in phase 5 rather than made a control: five presets and
57	    /// one broadcast-standard ceiling is what people actually pick, the sheet
58	    /// is already six control rows deep, and the `export` tool keeps
59	    /// `peak_dbtp` for a script that needs −0.3 or −2.0. The hint says the
60	    /// number, so a fixed value is visible rather than folklore.
61	    static let peakCeilingDBTP: Double = -1
62	
63	    /// A target as its menu row reads. The two named tiers say who asks for
64	    /// them, because "−14" and "−23" mean nothing to someone who has not met
65	    /// them before and everything to someone who has.
66	    ///
67	    /// Here rather than beside the popup it titles, and the move is the size
68	    /// payment `ExportSheetController.swift` owed before phase 7 put a Preset
69	    /// row and a burn-in on it. It belongs in this half by this file's own
70	    /// rule: it is a pure function of a target, holds no state, asks no
71	    /// control anything, and is `rateText`'s sibling — the spelling of one of
72	    /// the ladders `loudnessTargets` and `tiers` declare a few lines up.
73	    static func loudnessTitle(_ target: Double) -> String {
74	        let value = String(format: "%.0f", target).replacingOccurrences(of: "-", with: "−")
75	        switch target {
76	        case -14: return "\(value) LUFS (streaming)"
77	        case -23: return "\(value) LUFS (broadcast)"
78	        default: return "\(value) LUFS"
79	        }
80	    }

82	    /// What the core will take: `export_overrides.rs`'s own bounds for
83	    /// `loudness_lufs`, spelled here so the field's formatter refuses what
84	    /// the core would refuse rather than sending it and reading the message
85	    /// back.

88	    // MARK: - Quality
89	
90	    /// One row of the Quality popup: a video rate expressed as bits per pixel
91	    /// per frame, and the AAC rate that goes with it.
92	    ///
93	    /// **Where the video numbers come from.** They are anchored on one
94	    /// published figure and scaled from it rather than guessed: YouTube's
95	    /// recommended upload for 1080p SDR H.264 at 30 fps is 8 Mbps, and
96	    /// 1920 × 1080 × 30 is 62.2 Mpixel/s, so "High" is 8 000 000 / 62 200 000
97	    /// ≈ 0.129 bits per pixel per frame. The other three tiers are 0.5×,
98	    /// 0.75× and 1.5× of it — 4, 6 and 12 Mbps at 1080p30, which brackets
99	    /// Apple's HLS Authoring Specification 1080p H.264 rung (6.0–7.8 Mbps)
100	    /// on both sides.
101	    ///
102	    /// Holding bits-per-pixel constant makes the rate scale with the frame's
103	    /// area, so High is 3.6 Mbps at 720p and 32 Mbps at 4K. That is
104	    /// deliberately flatter than YouTube's own ladder, which is generous at
105	    /// the small end because its rungs are transcode targets; a master at a
106	    /// constant bits-per-pixel is the same picture at every size, which is
107	    /// what choosing "High" ought to mean.
108	    struct QualityTier {
109	        let name: String
110	        /// Bits per pixel per frame, for H.264 at 30 fps or less.
111	        let bitsPerPixel: Double
112	        /// AAC-LC stereo, bits per second. 128 kbps is the streaming
113	        /// baseline, 256 is what Apple Music ships, and 320 is where AAC-LC
114	        /// stops paying for the extra bits.
115	        let audioBitsPerSecond: Int
116	
117	        /// The video rate for a `width` × `height` frame at `fps`.
118	        ///
119	        /// The 30 is not a stand-in for `fps`: the frame rate enters through
120	        /// `rateFactor` instead, because bits do not scale linearly with it.
121	        /// Consecutive frames are more alike the closer together they are,
122	        /// which is why YouTube's ladder asks 1.5× for its 48–60 fps column
123	        /// and nothing extra for 24 fps over 30. This mirrors that shape —
124	        /// one step at 30 and below, one above it.
125	        func videoBitsPerSecond(width: Int, height: Int, fps: Fps, codec: String) -> Int {
126	            let pixels = Double(max(width, 1)) * Double(max(height, 1))
127	            let rateFactor = fps.double > 30.5 ? 1.5 : 1.0
128	            // HEVC reaches the same picture at roughly 60 % of H.264's rate —
129	            // the ratio between the two 1080p rungs of the same Apple
130	            // specification the tiers are calibrated against. AV1 takes
131	            // HEVC's factor (spec §11 CX-9 (2)): its efficiency goes to the
132	            // picture, not the file size. VP9 takes it too (CX-9 (2), CX-16 (7)).
133	            let lower = codec.lowercased()
134	            let codecFactor = QualityTier.isHEVC(codec) || lower == "av1" || lower == "vp9"
135	                ? 0.6 : 1.0
136	            let bits = pixels * 30 * bitsPerPixel * rateFactor * codecFactor
137	            // To the nearest 100 kbps: these are estimates, and a request for
138	            // "7 963 200 bits" would claim a precision they do not have.
139	            return max(100_000, Int((bits / 100_000).rounded()) * 100_000)
140	        }
141	
142	        private static func isHEVC(_ codec: String) -> Bool {
143	            let codec = codec.lowercased()
144	            return codec.hasPrefix("hevc") || codec.hasPrefix("h265") || codec.hasPrefix("h.265")
145	        }
146	    }

150	    /// session's ladder when it carries none.
151	    static let tiers: [QualityTier] = [
152	        QualityTier(name: "Low", bitsPerPixel: 0.064, audioBitsPerSecond: 128_000),
153	        QualityTier(name: "Medium", bitsPerPixel: 0.096, audioBitsPerSecond: 192_000),
154	        QualityTier(name: "High", bitsPerPixel: 0.129, audioBitsPerSecond: 256_000),
155	        QualityTier(name: "Maximum", bitsPerPixel: 0.193, audioBitsPerSecond: 320_000),
156	    ]

160	    /// Both the enablement of every control AND every override key are read
161	    /// from one of these, so a greyed-out control can never still be sending
162	    /// a value to the core — which is what keeps the sheet honest as formats
163	    /// that are not H.264 movies join the list.
164	    struct Applies {
165	        private let preset: ExportPreset?
166	
167	        init(_ preset: ExportPreset?) {
168	            self.preset = preset
169	        }
170	
171	        /// A frame sequence — GIF or APNG — has a size and a frame rate but
172	        /// no bit rate to spend and no audio track to put one on.
173	        private var frameSequence: Bool {
174	            guard let preset = preset else { return false }
175	            return ExportSheetController.isFrameSequence(container: preset.container)
176	        }
177	
178	        /// A row whose data rate is not the sheet's to name. ProRes is a
179	        /// fixed-rate intra codec — the profile decides — and §7.8's preset
180	        /// pairs it with LPCM audio; the two LPCM audio rows are
181	        /// uncompressed by definition, so offering either of them an AAC bit
182	        /// rate would be a control that changes nothing about the file. Both
183	        /// are `ExportSettings.carriesLinearPCM(codec:)`.
184	        private var fixedRate: Bool {
185	            ExportSettings.carriesLinearPCM(codec: preset?.codec ?? "")
186	        }
187	
188	        private var hasVideo: Bool { preset.map { !$0.audioOnly } ?? false }
189	
190	        var size: Bool { hasVideo }
191	        var frameRate: Bool { hasVideo }
192	        var videoBitrate: Bool { hasVideo && !frameSequence && !fixedRate }
193	        var audioBitrate: Bool { preset != nil && !frameSequence && !fixedRate }
194	        var quality: Bool { videoBitrate || audioBitrate }
195	
196	        /// Loudness normalisation is a gain on the mixed sound, so it
197	        /// applies to every row that HAS sound — which is every row but the
198	        /// two frame sequences. Deliberately not gated by `fixedRate` (ProRes
199	        /// carries LPCM audio and takes a gain like anything else) nor by
200	        /// `hasVideo` (the three audio-only rows are exactly where a
201	        /// delivery target matters most).
202	        var loudness: Bool { preset != nil && !frameSequence }
203	
204	        /// The Dynamic Range popup is live only on a row that carries an HLG
205	        /// project's HDR picture (spec §11 HD-14 (h)).
206	        var dynamicRange: Bool { preset?.carriesHDR ?? false }
207	
208	        /// The Speed popup is live only on a row whose bundled encoder has
209	        /// speeds (spec §11 CX-12 (2); not `vp9_webm`, CX-16 (2)).
210	        var encoderSpeed: Bool { !(preset?.encoderSpeeds.isEmpty ?? true) }
211	
212	        /// The Bit depth popup is live only on a row that lists depths: the
213	        /// uncompressed WAV and AIFF rows (spec §11 AU-29).
214	        var audioBits: Bool { !(preset?.audioBits.isEmpty ?? true) }
215	
216	        /// The Stems popup is live only on a row that lists modes: the three
217	        /// audio rows (spec §11 AU-108 (a)).
218	        var stems: Bool { !(preset?.stems.isEmpty ?? true) }
219	
220	        /// The video rate is a soft cap on every row a bundled encoder writes
221	        /// (spec §11 CX-13, CX-16 (7)), whether or not it has speeds.
222	        var softCap: Bool { preset?.writer != nil }
223	    }
224	
225	    /// GIF and APNG. Spelled once, and taken from the container rather than
226	    /// the codec because that is the field both `ExportPreset` and
227	    /// `ExportSettings` carry.
228	    static func isFrameSequence(container: String) -> Bool {
229	        let container = container.lowercased()
230	        return container == "gif" || container == "apng"
231	    }
232	
233	    /// A bit rate as the tier rows and the footnote spell it.
234	    static func rateText(_ bitsPerSecond: Int) -> String {
235	        if bitsPerSecond >= 1_000_000 {
236	            return String(format: "%.1f Mbps", Double(bitsPerSecond) / 1_000_000)
237	        }
238	        return "\(Int((Double(bitsPerSecond) / 1000).rounded())) kbps"
239	    }
240	}
241

1	import AppKit
2	import UniformTypeIdentifiers
3	
4	/// The export card's two commits, Export… and Add to Queue, which end in a save panel and hand
5	/// the resolved settings to the editor: `commit(queue:)` with the three button actions that
6	/// reach it, `recipeOptions`, `suggestedName` and `panelMessage`. An extension of
7	/// `ExportSheetController` in a file of its own, a pure move out of the controller before the
8	/// HDR road map's export range (hdr H-0).
9	extension ExportSheetController {
10	    // MARK: - Commit
11	
12	    @objc func cancelClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
13	        dismiss(self)
14	    }
15	
16	    /// Export… — write it now, behind a progress sheet.
17	    @objc func exportClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
18	        commit(queue: false)
19	    }
20	
21	    /// Add to Queue — write it later, behind nothing. The SAME commit, in one
22	    /// method, so the buttons cannot drift (road map 2's phase 7e).
23	    @objc func queueClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
24	        commit(queue: true)
25	    }
26	
27	    /// Hands off to the save panel, then to `EditorViewController`'s
28	    /// `beginExport` — or, for Add to Queue, its `enqueueExport`. The settings
29	    /// are captured BEFORE the dismissal: after it this controller's window is
30	    /// gone and its controls are on their way out of the view tree. Everything
31	    /// above the handoff is the same for both buttons and is written once for
32	    /// that reason: a queued job is not a second kind of export, it is this
33	    /// one held until its turn.
34	    private func commit(queue: Bool) {
35	        // End any edit in a Custom field first. A mouse click on a button
36	        // does not take the first responder from a text field, so the value
37	        // typed there has not been committed — `controlTextDidEndEditing`,
38	        // and the resolve it runs, fire only when the field editor resigns —
39	        // and `resolved` still describes the size from BEFORE the edit.
40	        // Handing the first responder to nobody makes it resign now,
41	        // synchronously, so the read below sees the numbers on screen. A
42	        // field whose text its formatter rejects refuses to resign; that is
43	        // the person's to fix, so the click just beeps.
44	        guard endSheetFieldEditing() else { return }
45	        guard let editor = editor, let settings = resolved,
46	              let window = editor.view.window
47	        else {
48	            NSSound.beep()
49	            return
50	        }
51	        // Read while the controls still exist. `recipeOptions` is not part of
52	        // `settings` and never can be: the burn-in changes the PICTURE, so it
53	        // travels with the description of the picture rather than through the
54	        // override table, which drops a key it does not know without a word
55	        // (`RecipeOptions`).
56	        let options = recipeOptions
57	        // Remembered on the COMMIT and not on the dismissal: a card somebody
58	        // opened, fiddled with and cancelled is not a choice they made — and
59	        // queueing a job is as much a choice as exporting one, so both
60	        // buttons record it.
61	        currentChoice.remember()
62	        let name = suggestedName(for: settings, in: editor)
63	        dismiss(self)
64	
65	        let panel = NSSavePanel()
66	        panel.nameFieldStringValue = name
67	        panel.canCreateDirectories = true
68	        panel.isExtensionHidden = false
69	        panel.message = Self.panelMessage(for: settings)
70	        if let type = Exporter.contentType(for: settings) {
71	            panel.allowedContentTypes = [type]
72	        }
73	        // AppKit queues this behind the sheet that is on its way out, so the
74	        // panel appears once the settings card has finished leaving.
75	        panel.beginSheetModal(for: window) { [weak editor] response in
76	            guard response == .OK, let url = panel.url, let editor = editor else { return }
77	            // The handoff, and the only place the two buttons differ. The
78	            // project and its media are read on the far side of it, at the
79	            // moment the destination is known — which for a queued job is the
80	            // whole of what makes it immutable (`ExportQueueController`).
81	            if queue {
82	                editor.enqueueExport(settings: settings, to: url, options: options)
83	            } else {
84	                editor.beginExport(settings: settings, to: url, options: options)
85	            }
86	        }
87	    }
88	
89	    /// What the card asks of the RECIPE rather than of the export settings —
90	    /// today, the burn-in and nothing else.
91	    var recipeOptions: RecipeOptions {
92	        RecipeOptions(burnInTimecode: burnInCheckbox.state == .on)
93	    }
94	
95	    /// The document's name with the container's extension: `displayStem`, the
96	    /// title with the package's own extension off and NOTHING else off, so
97	    /// "Board v1.2" is `Board v1.2.mp4` (`ProjectDocument+DisplayStem.swift`).
98	    private func suggestedName(for settings: ExportSettings, in editor: EditorViewController)
99	        -> String
100	    {
101	        let stem = editor.document?.displayStem ?? ProjectDocument.untitledDisplayName
102	        return stem + "." + Exporter.fileExtension(for: settings)
103	    }
104	
105	    /// The save panel's one line about what is being written. "As a movie"
106	    /// was wrong for half the table: a GIF or an APNG is an animated image
107	    /// and the audio-only row writes no picture at all. The classes are the
108	    /// sheet's own (`Applies`, `isFrameSequence`), so a format that is
109	    /// neither is a movie by the same reading that gave it a Size popup.
110	    private static func panelMessage(for settings: ExportSettings) -> String {
111	        if settings.isAudioOnly { return "Export the timeline's audio." }
112	        if isFrameSequence(container: settings.container) {
113	            return "Export the timeline as an animated \(settings.container.uppercased())."
114	        }
115	        return "Export the timeline as a movie."
116	    }
117	}

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, and `engines` in `package.json` sets the Node it needs. `README.md` has
the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

</system-reminder>

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,

  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s

  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),

  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join;

  `rc_agent_string_create` (CJ0d's T15c), a plain static because the trampoline

  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are `ReelCore+Graphics.swift`'s: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,

  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library

  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a

  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and

  cursor file: its bookmark when it resolves, else the stored path, existing or
  not), `isTrashed` and

  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-nine op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

    /// frame at whatever tick is requested, so nothing else has to know.
    static func videoComposition(
        _ built: BuiltComposition, settings: ExportSettings
    ) -> AVVideoComposition {
        let fps = settings.fps
        var configuration = built.videoConfiguration
        guard fps.num > 0, fps.den > 0 else { return built.videoComposition }
        configuration.frameDuration = CompositionBuilder.frameDuration(fps)
        guard configuration.frameDuration != built.videoConfiguration.frameDuration
        else { return built.videoComposition }
        return AVVideoComposition(configuration: configuration)

140	    /// the two look alike. Whether a file can hold a sound track is decided
141	    /// by the container's format — a GIF has no audio track to put samples
142	    /// in whatever you encode — so it is answered once for the container.
143	    /// A fourth channel is decided by the CODEC: `Container::Mov` hosts
144	    /// `prores_422` and `prores_4444` alike, and 422 cannot carry alpha at
145	    /// any bitrate, so a container-level answer would have to be wrong for
146	    /// one of the two rows. Same shape of fact, different owner.
147	    ///
148	    /// **`gif` is false and `apng` is true, and the difference is the word
149	    /// CHANNEL.** Both can show a transparent pixel, so both look alike
150	    /// from the outside and a reader who has exported one will call this
151	    /// row a mistake. APNG is true colour with a real fourth channel and a
152	    /// pixel may be any fraction of opaque. A GIF has ONE palette index
153	    /// nominated as transparent: a pixel is either that index or fully
154	    /// opaque, there is no partial value to store, and a soft edge against
155	    /// nothing comes out as a hard jagged one. A flag that answered "yes"
156	    /// for both would license the sheet to promise a translucent GIF.
157	    /// Measured on the way in, not assumed: an `apng` export of a
158	    /// transparent canvas decodes `pix_fmt=rgba` with its corner at
159	    /// alpha 0, and a `gif` of the same timeline decodes with the corner
160	    /// transparent through its palette and no partial value anywhere.
161	    pub(crate) alpha: bool,
162	    /// `None` means "the project's canvas size", which is what every movie
163	    /// row wants: a preset is an encoding, and the size is the document's
164	    /// unless a `width`/`height` override says otherwise. The resolver
165	    /// fills the canvas in for the audio-only rows too, so every settings
166	    /// object carries a width. Only the two image rows pin one — the cap
167	    /// `Project::export_sizes` lists as their default.
168	    pub(crate) size: Option<(u32, u32)>,
169	    /// `None` means "the project's canvas rate", which is what every movie
170	    /// preset wants. Only the image-sequence rows pin one, because their
171	    /// cost is frames × pixels and nothing else.
172	    pub(crate) fps: Option<Fps>,
173	    /// The `AVAssetExportSession` preset name, verbatim; `None` for a
174	    /// container AVFoundation cannot write.
175	    ///
176	    /// Since phase 5 the field means only **"AVFoundation can write this
177	    /// row"**, and the name itself is a record rather than an instruction.
178	    /// Nothing has run a session since M2, but `null` here is still the
179	    /// one thing routing an export to the ImageIO writer
180	    /// (`ExportSettings.isImageSequence` is literally `avPreset == nil`),
181	    /// so a row that AVFoundation writes must carry SOME name even when
182	    /// AVFoundation has no name for it. There is no `AVAssetExportPreset`
183	    /// for LPCM in a WAV or an AIFF, so those two rows carry the audio-only
184	    /// name `audio_m4a` carries: it is the closest true statement
185	    /// available — "an audio-only file AVFoundation writes" — and a null
186	    /// there would hand a WAV to `ImageSequenceWriter`, which would refuse
187	    /// it as an unknown image container and report a format this table
188	    /// advertises as unsupported. A name also means "the composition is
189	    /// read back through AVFoundation" (spec §11 CX-15), which is all it says
190	    /// on `av1_webm` and `vp9_webm`, whose files the core writes.
191	    pub(crate) avf_preset: Option<&'static str>,
192	    /// The bundled encoder that writes the row's video, or `None` for
193	    /// AVFoundation's own encoders (ImageIO where `avf_preset` is null).
194	    /// A row with a writer takes `encoder_speed` when its encoder has
195	    /// speeds (`Writer::takes_speed`).
196	    pub(crate) writer: Option<Writer>,
197	}

199	/// A rate as the two-element `[num, den]` array the spec spells every rate
200	/// with, or null for "the project's own". One function so the preset row
201	/// and the resolved settings cannot disagree about the shape.
202	pub(crate) fn fps_json(fps: Option<Fps>) -> Value {
203	    match fps {
204	        Some(fps) => Value::Array(vec![Value::from(fps.num), Value::from(fps.den)]),
205	        None => Value::Null,
206	    }
207	}
