209	impl Preset {
210	    /// True for the rows written frame by frame through ImageIO — the ones
211	    /// with no session preset — whose picture is FITTED inside the size
212	    /// rather than letterboxed to it, so a size on them is a box and the
213	    /// resolved numbers are the fit (`export_size::fit_within`).
214	    pub(crate) fn fits_inside_size(&self) -> bool {
215	        self.video && self.avf_preset.is_none()
216	    }
217	
218	    /// True for the rows whose frame has to have EVEN pixel dimensions:
219	    /// every row AVFoundation writes but ProRes 4444 (spec §11 G-33). On
220	    /// these an odd edge is resolved one pixel smaller, in the size list's
221	    /// Document row and in the resolved settings alike
222	    /// (`export_size::even_size`), so the size reported is the size the
223	    /// writer writes.
224	    ///
225	    /// It is asked of `avf_preset` and the codec rather than listed row by
226	    /// row, so a new AVFoundation row is even-sized until someone exempts
227	    /// it — the safe side, since 4:2:0 chroma needs it and a row that can
228	    /// keep an odd edge has to be measured doing so, as ProRes 4444 was
229	    /// (`ExporterWriter+Settings.swift`'s `encodedSize`). The audio-only
230	    /// rows answer true: they have no picture and go on reporting what
231	    /// `h264` reports. The two image rows answer false; their numbers are
232	    /// the fit (`fits_inside_size`), odd or not.
233	    pub(crate) fn even_sized(&self) -> bool {
234	        self.avf_preset.is_some() && self.codec != "prores4444"
235	    }
236	
237	    /// True for a row whose bundled encoder has speeds, the rows
238	    /// `encoder_speed` applies to (spec §11 CX-12 (2), CX-16 (2)).
239	    pub(crate) fn takes_encoder_speed(&self) -> bool {
240	        self.writer.is_some_and(Writer::takes_speed)
241	    }
242	
243	    /// True for the uncompressed audio rows, `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff`,
244	    /// the rows `audio_bits` applies to (spec §11 AU-29). ProRes's LPCM
245	    /// track keeps 16 bits; it is not an `lpcm` row.
246	    pub(crate) fn takes_audio_bits(&self) -> bool {
247	        self.codec == "lpcm"
248	    }
249	
250	    /// True for the three audio-only rows, `audio_m4a`, `audio_wav` and
251	    /// `audio_aiff`, the rows `stems` applies to (spec §11 AU-108 (a)).
252	    pub(crate) fn takes_stems(&self) -> bool {
253	        !self.video
254	    }
255	
256	    pub(crate) fn to_json(&self) -> Value {
257	        let mut out = Map::new();
258	        out.insert("id".to_string(), Value::from(self.id));
259	        out.insert("name".to_string(), Value::from(self.name));
260	        out.insert(
261	            "container".to_string(),
262	            Value::from(self.container.as_str()),
263	        );
264	        out.insert("codec".to_string(), Value::from(self.codec));
265	        out.insert("video".to_string(), Value::from(self.video));
266	        out.insert(
267	            "size".to_string(),
268	            match self.size {
269	                Some((w, h)) => Value::Array(vec![Value::from(w), Value::from(h)]),
270	                None => Value::Null,
271	            },
272	        );
273	        // `size` and `fps` are spelled the same way for the same reason:
274	        // null is "whatever the project is" — the document size, the
275	        // document rate — which the resolver fills in from the canvas.
276	        out.insert("fps".to_string(), fps_json(self.fps));
277	        out.insert(
278	            "avf_preset".to_string(),
279	            match self.avf_preset {
280	                Some(name) => Value::from(name),
281	                None => Value::Null,
282	            },
283	        );
284	        if crate::dynamic_range::HDR_ROWS.contains(&self.id) {
285	            out.insert("hdr".to_string(), Value::from(true));
286	        }
287	        if let Some(writer) = self.writer {
288	            out.insert("writer".to_string(), Value::from(writer.as_str()));
289	            if writer.takes_speed() {
290	                let speeds = EncoderSpeed::ALL.iter().map(|s| Value::from(s.as_str()));
291	                out.insert("encoder_speeds".to_string(), speeds.collect());
292	            }
293	        }
294	        if self.takes_audio_bits() {
295	            let bits = [16, 24].iter().map(|b| Value::from(*b));
296	            out.insert("audio_bits".to_string(), bits.collect());
297	        }
298	        if self.takes_stems() {
299	            let modes = ["tracks", "names"].iter().map(|m| Value::from(*m));
300	            out.insert("stems".to_string(), modes.collect());
301	        }
302	        Value::Object(out)
303	    }
304	}
305	//! The containers Frame Job writes (spec §7.8), and the four questions
306	//! each one answers about ITSELF: its extension, its UTI, whether a
307	//! leading index is worth rewriting, whether it can hold sound at all.
308	//!
309	//! Moved whole out of `export_table.rs` under the size rule (core/CLAUDE.md:
310	//! a module at ~600 lines gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on),
311	//! as codec-export C1's toll T1, a pure move. `export_table.rs` re-exports
312	//! [`Container`], so every `crate::export_table::Container` path holds.
313	
314	/// The containers Frame Job writes. Kept as an enum rather than a string so
315	/// the container, its UTI, its network-optimization default and whether it
316	/// can hold sound at all are decided in exactly one exhaustive place.
317	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
318	pub(crate) enum Container {
319	    Mov,
320	    Mp4,
321	    M4a,
322	    Wav,
323	    Aiff,
324	    Gif,
325	    Apng,
326	    /// WebM, written by the core's own writer (`webm_writer.rs`, spec §11
327	    /// CX-15), not by AVFoundation.
328	    Webm,
329	}
330	
331	impl Container {
332	    pub(crate) fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
333	        match self {
334	            Container::Mov => "mov",
335	            Container::Mp4 => "mp4",
336	            Container::M4a => "m4a",
337	            Container::Wav => "wav",
338	            Container::Aiff => "aiff",
339	            Container::Gif => "gif",
340	            Container::Apng => "apng",
341	            Container::Webm => "webm",
342	        }
343	    }
344	
345	    /// The output file's UTI. On the AVFoundation path Swift passes this
346	    /// straight to `outputFileType`, whose raw values ARE UTIs; on the
347	    /// ImageIO path it is the destination type
348	    /// `CGImageDestinationCreateWithURL` takes. Either way it is what the
349	    /// save panel's content type and file extension are derived from, which
350	    /// is why the two image formats name a real UTI here rather than
351	    /// nothing — an export that could not tell the panel it writes a `.gif`
352	    /// would be worse off than one whose type string a session would
353	    /// reject, and a session is never built for them.
354	    ///
355	    /// An APNG is written to an ordinary PNG destination — the animation
356	    /// lives in `acTL`/`fcTL` chunks inside a file that is still a PNG — so
357	    /// its type identifier is PNG's, not one of its own.
358	    ///
359	    /// The two LPCM rows' identifiers are exactly `AVFileType.wav` and
360	    /// `AVFileType.aiff`'s raw values, which is what lets
361	    /// `Exporter.fileType(for:)` resolve them from this string alone
362	    /// rather than growing a container list of its own.
363	    pub(crate) fn file_type(self) -> &'static str {
364	        match self {
365	            Container::Mov => "com.apple.quicktime-movie",
366	            Container::Mp4 => "public.mpeg-4",
367	            Container::M4a => "com.apple.m4a-audio",
368	            Container::Wav => "com.microsoft.waveform-audio",
369	            Container::Aiff => "public.aiff-audio",
370	            Container::Gif => "com.compuserve.gif",
371	            Container::Apng => "public.png",
372	            Container::Webm => "org.webmproject.webm",
373	        }
374	    }
375	
376	    /// Whether `shouldOptimizeForNetworkUse` defaults on. MP4 and M4A are
377	    /// the delivery containers people upload, and a leading `moov` atom
378	    /// lets a player start before the file is fully fetched. A ProRes MOV
379	    /// is an editing master handed to another application, where the
380	    /// rewrite pass buys nothing. An HEVC-with-alpha MOV is a delivery file
381	    /// too, and its default stays off all the same: that was the owner's
382	    /// choice for the row (spec §11 G-33), and the override turns it on. GIF
383	    /// and APNG have no `moov` atom and nothing to move: a viewer already
384	    /// starts on the first frame, and
385	    /// neither do WAV and AIFF — a RIFF or an IFF file is a header
386	    /// followed by samples, with no index to relocate, so the flag would
387	    /// be a request the writer has nothing to do about. A WebM's index (its
388	    /// SeekHead) is already at the front, so the flag is off and inert there
389	    /// too (spec §11 CX-15 (1)).
390	    pub(crate) fn optimizes_for_network(self) -> bool {
391	        matches!(self, Container::Mp4 | Container::M4a)
392	    }
393	
394	    /// Whether the container can hold sound. Every movie container can,
395	    /// and M4A, WAV and AIFF are nothing else; GIF and APNG are picture
396	    /// formats with no audio track in the file format at all, so
397	    /// `audio: false` for those is a fact about the container rather than
398	    /// a decision about the project.
399	    pub(crate) fn carries_audio(self) -> bool {
400	        !matches!(self, Container::Gif | Container::Apng)
401	    }
402	}
403	//! The output sizes the export sheet offers for one document and one
404	//! format — `rc_export_sizes` (spec §7.8) — and the one rule for what a
405	//! size MEANS on an image format, which `export_settings` applies too.
406	//!
407	//! A preset is an encoding and carries no size (`export.rs`), so the size
408	//! is a second choice, and this module is the list that choice is made
409	//! from: the format's cap if it has one, the document's own size, and the
410	//! standard sizes fitted to the document's aspect. The FIRST row is the
411	//! default — the rule every list the export sheet is built from follows —
412	//! which is the document's size for a movie format and the cap for an
413	//! image format, because an image format's cap is the point of the row
414	//! and not a ceiling that only applies from above.
415	//!
416	//! **The number is the short edge.** A standard size is named by one
417	//! number, and the number people use is the short one: "1080p ultrawide"
418	//! is 2560 × 1080 and "1080p vertical" is 1080 × 1920, and both are 1080p
419	//! to everyone who says it. Naming by the long edge would call the
420	//! ultrawide 2560p and the vertical 1920p, which nobody does. So a row
421	//! keeps its short edge exactly and the long edge follows the document:
422	//! L = S × long / short of the document, on whichever axis the document is
423	//! longer along, and S × S for a square.
424	//!
425	//! **The long edge is rounded to even.** 4:2:0 chroma puts one colour
426	//! sample under each 2 × 2 block of luma, so H.264 and HEVC want even
427	//! dimensions, and `ExporterWriter.evenDimension` rounds an odd one down
428	//! before writing. Rounding here — to the nearest even integer, a tie
429	//! going up — means the size the popup shows is the size the file has;
430	//! leaving it to the writer would change the size behind the sheet's
431	//! back.
432	//!
433	//! **The even rule (spec §11 G-33).** The same is true of the document row
434	//! and of any size asked for, so on every row that needs even dimensions
435	//! (`Preset::even_sized`: every row AVFoundation writes but ProRes 4444)
436	//! the size is resolved HERE, by [`even_size`]: the document row's numbers
437	//! in this list, and in `export_settings` whatever was asked. An odd edge
438	//! is one pixel SMALLER. Down, because that is the size the writer already
439	//! wrote, so the report moves to the file and no file changes size;
440	//! because rounding up would hand the encoder a frame larger than the
441	//! picture on that axis; and because every listed row is then its own
442	//! fixed point, as an image format's is. The row is named "Document
443	//! (even)" when its numbers are not the canvas's, which is the whole of
444	//! how the popup says why. The argument this replaces was that a "Document
445	//! size" that was not the document's size would be a lie; the lie was the
446	//! row that said 321 × 181 over a file of 320 × 180. ProRes 4444 and the
447	//! two image formats keep an odd edge, and their row is "Document size",
448	//! the canvas as it is.
449	//!
450	//! **An image format's numbers are the file's.** A GIF or an APNG is
451	//! written frame by frame with the picture FITTED inside the size — aspect
452	//! kept, never upscaled — where a movie is letterboxed to exactly the frame
453	//! asked for (`ExporterImageSequence`, spec §7.8): padding costs bytes in
454	//! every frame for pixels that carry nothing, and a bigger frame carries no
455	//! more detail. So on those two formats every row here, and every size
456	//! `export_settings` resolves — the cap, a standard row, a custom size — is
457	//! the canvas fitted inside that box ([`fit_within`]), so that the popup,
458	//! the sheet's readout and the `export` tool all report the numbers the
459	//! file will have: a vertical 1080 × 1920 timeline's "GIF default" is
460	//! 152 × 270, not 480 × 270. The fit is decided here, once; the writer
461	//! draws each frame at exactly this size and does not fit a second time.
462	//! It is also its own fixed point — a fitted size fed back as the box
463	//! fits to itself — because that is exactly what happens: the sheet and
464	//! the tool send a listed row's numbers back through `export_settings` as
465	//! `width` and `height`, and a fit that could move a derived edge by a
466	//! pixel on the second pass would show one size and write another.
467	//!
468	//! **Rows may repeat.** A 1920 × 1080 document's 1080p row IS the document
469	//! row, and on a 1080 × 1920 document every image-format row from 1080p up
470	//! is the document again. They are listed anyway, because an id is the
471	//! `export` tool's vocabulary and a request for `1080p` has to mean the
472	//! same thing on every document — refusing it exactly where it is a no-op
473	//! would be the popup's tidiness leaking into an API. The sheet hides a
474	//! row whose numbers an earlier row already has, so a person never sees one
475	//! size under two names, and the row that shows is the one whose name says
476	//! more ("Document size" over "1080p"). Rows larger than the document are
477	//! offered for a movie — they were before, as the 4K preset — because a
478	//! 720p screen recording exported at 4K for a platform that picks its
479	//! bitrate by resolution is a real request.
480	
481	use serde_json::{Map, Value};
482	
483	use crate::export;
484	use crate::model::Project;
485	
486	/// The standard sizes, largest first, as (id, name, short edge). The id is
487	/// the `export` tool's vocabulary and the name is the popup's; they differ
488	/// only for 4K, which nobody calls 2160p out loud but which needs a
489	/// short-edge id to sit in the same vocabulary as the other three.
490	const STANDARD: [(&str, &str, u32); 4] = [
491	    ("2160p", "4K", 2160),
492	    ("1440p", "1440p", 1440),
493	    ("1080p", "1080p", 1080),
494	    ("720p", "720p", 720),
495	];
496	
497	/// One row of the list, before it is JSON.
498	struct Row {
499	    id: &'static str,
500	    name: String,
501	    width: u32,
502	    height: u32,
503	}
504	
505	impl Row {
506	    fn to_json(&self) -> Value {
507	        let mut out = Map::new();
508	        out.insert("id".to_string(), Value::from(self.id));
509	        out.insert("name".to_string(), Value::from(self.name.as_str()));
510	        out.insert("width".to_string(), Value::from(self.width));
511	        out.insert("height".to_string(), Value::from(self.height));
512	        Value::Object(out)
513	    }
514	}

516	impl Project {
517	    /// The sizes the export sheet offers for `preset_id` against this
518	    /// document, as the JSON array of `{id, name, width, height}` rows
519	    /// `rc_export_sizes` returns, in menu order — the first is the default.
520	    ///
521	    /// The rows:
522	    ///
523	    /// 1. `preset` — the format's cap, "GIF default" / "APNG default", for
524	    ///    the two rows of the table that carry one; nothing for the rest.
525	    /// 2. `document` — "Document size", the canvas as it is; on a row that
526	    ///    needs even dimensions the canvas evened ([`even_size`]), named
527	    ///    "Document (even)" when that is not the canvas's own size.
528	    /// 3. `2160p` ("4K"), `1440p`, `1080p`, `720p` — the short edge named,
529	    ///    the long edge fitted to the canvas and rounded to even.
530	    ///
531	    /// On an image format every row's numbers are the canvas fitted inside
532	    /// that row's box, never upscaled — the size the file will have. Rows
533	    /// may repeat an earlier row's numbers and are listed anyway (the
534	    /// module doc says why); the sheet hides the repeats.
535	    ///
536	    /// One list for every movie format, the audio-only row included: a
537	    /// width is reported for it the way `export_settings` reports one, and
538	    /// the sheet disables the control rather than this module keeping a
539	    /// second rule for one row. `Err` for an unknown preset, naming it —
540	    /// the same lookup and the same words as `export_settings`.
541	    pub fn export_sizes(&self, preset_id: &str) -> Result<Value, String> {
542	        let preset = export::preset(preset_id)?;
543	        let document = (self.canvas.width, self.canvas.height);
544	        let fits = preset.fits_inside_size();
545	        let sized = |(width, height): (u32, u32)| {
546	            if fits {
547	                fit_within(document, (width, height))
548	            } else {
549	                (width, height)
550	            }
551	        };
552	
553	        let mut rows: Vec<Row> = Vec::new();
554	        if let Some(cap) = preset.size {
555	            // The codec in capitals is the format's name as people write
556	            // it — GIF, APNG — for the two rows that carry a cap.
557	            let (width, height) = sized(cap);
558	            rows.push(Row {
559	                id: "preset",
560	                name: format!("{} default", preset.codec.to_uppercase()),
561	                width,
562	                height,
563	            });
564	        }
565	        // The id is `document` either way: the name is the popup's, and it
566	        // changes only when the numbers are not the canvas's.
567	        let listed = if preset.even_sized() {
568	            even_size(document)
569	        } else {
570	            document
571	        };
572	        let name = if listed == document {
573	            "Document size"
574	        } else {
575	            "Document (even)"
576	        };
577	        rows.push(Row {
578	            id: "document",
579	            name: name.to_string(),
580	            width: listed.0,
581	            height: listed.1,
582	        });
583	        for (id, name, short) in STANDARD {
584	            let (width, height) = sized(fitted(document, short));
585	            rows.push(Row {
586	                id,
587	                name: name.to_string(),
588	                width,
589	                height,
590	            });
591	        }
592	
593	        Ok(Value::Array(rows.iter().map(Row::to_json).collect()))
594	    }
595	}
596	
597	/// The size whose short edge is `short`, in the aspect of a `width` ×
598	/// `height` document: the long edge is `short` × the document's long edge
599	/// over its short one, rounded to the nearest even integer with a tie
600	/// going up, on the axis the document is longer along. A square document
601	/// gives `short` × `short`.
602	fn fitted((width, height): (u32, u32), short: u32) -> (u32, u32) {
603	    let doc_long = u64::from(width.max(height));
604	    // `validate` refuses a zero edge; the `max` keeps the division total
605	    // regardless, since no input may panic.
606	    let doc_short = u64::from(width.min(height)).max(1);
607	
608	    // The nearest even integer to short × doc_long / doc_short is twice
609	    // the nearest integer to half of it, and round(a / b) with a tie going
610	    // up is (2a + b) / 2b in integer division — here a = short × doc_long
611	    // and b = 2 × doc_short, so the whole thing is one division. u64
612	    // because a canvas need only be non-zero (`validate`), not inside
613	    // `set_canvas`'s 16..16384, so the product is not bounded by u32.
614	    let half = (u64::from(short) * doc_long + doc_short) / (2 * doc_short);
615	    // A canvas far outside those bounds can carry a ratio no u32 holds;
616	    // the row is then unusable, but a query must answer, and evenly.
617	    let long = u32::try_from(half * 2).unwrap_or(u32::MAX - 1);
618	
619	    if width >= height {
620	        (long, short)

626	/// A size as a row that needs even dimensions writes it (spec §11 G-33),
627	/// each edge on its own: below 2 it is 2, an odd edge is one SMALLER, and an
628	/// even edge is itself. The rule `export_settings` and
629	/// [`Project::export_sizes`] share, so the list and the resolver cannot
630	/// disagree about what an H.264 will measure; the module doc says why down.
631	/// It is `ExporterWriter.evenDimension`'s arithmetic, which stays as the
632	/// floor under any caller that did not come through here.
633	pub(crate) fn even_size((width, height): (u32, u32)) -> (u32, u32) {
634	    let even = |edge: u32| if edge < 2 { 2 } else { edge - edge % 2 };
635	    (even(width), even(height))

638	/// A `width` × `height` canvas fitted inside a box: the canvas itself when
639	/// it already fits — never upscaled — and otherwise scaled down, aspect
640	/// kept, so that the edge which meets the box first takes the box's value
641	/// exactly and the other is the scaled value rounded UP to a whole pixel.
642	/// The rule an image format's size means (module doc), shared by
643	/// `export_settings` and [`Project::export_sizes`] so the two cannot
644	/// disagree about what a GIF will measure.
645	///
646	/// Up rather than to the nearest, so that the fit is its own fixed point.
647	/// Fitting the result again compares box × canvas products on the two
648	/// axes, and the derived edge — never below its exact value — keeps the
649	/// same axis limiting, whose derived edge is the same ceiling; rounded to
650	/// the nearest it can fall below the exact value, flip the limiting axis
651	/// on the second pass, and take a pixel off the other edge (a 3024 × 1964
652	/// recording's 1080p box, 1662 × 1080, came back 1662 × 1079 and then
653	/// 1661 × 1079). The ceiling never leaves the box: the limiting axis is
654	/// the one whose exact scaled value fits, and a whole number no smaller
655	/// than a value that fits inside a whole box edge fits too.
656	pub(crate) fn fit_within((width, height): (u32, u32), (box_w, box_h): (u32, u32)) -> (u32, u32) {
657	    if width <= box_w && height <= box_h {
658	        return (width, height);
659	    }
660	    let (w, h) = (u64::from(width).max(1), u64::from(height).max(1));
661	    let (bw, bh) = (u64::from(box_w).max(1), u64::from(box_h).max(1));
662	    // The width meets the box first when box_w / w ≤ box_h / h, which is
663	    // box_w × h ≤ box_h × w with no division to round.
664	    let (fw, fh) = if bw * h <= bh * w {
665	        (bw, ceil_div(h * bw, w))
666	    } else {
667	        (ceil_div(w * bh, h), bh)
668	    };
669	    let edge = |value: u64| u32::try_from(value).unwrap_or(u32::MAX).max(1);
670	    (edge(fw), edge(fh))
671	}

274	        // null is "whatever the project is" — the document size, the

276	        out.insert("fps".to_string(), fps_json(self.fps));
277	        out.insert(

279	            match self.avf_preset {

281	                None => Value::Null,

305	//! The containers Frame Job writes (spec §7.8), and the four questions

314	/// The containers Frame Job writes. Kept as an enum rather than a string so
315	/// the container, its UTI, its network-optimization default and whether it
316	/// can hold sound at all are decided in exactly one exhaustive place.
317	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
318	pub(crate) enum Container {
319	    Mov,
320	    Mp4,
321	    M4a,
322	    Wav,
323	    Aiff,
324	    Gif,
325	    Apng,
326	    /// WebM, written by the core's own writer (`webm_writer.rs`, spec §11
327	    /// CX-15), not by AVFoundation.
328	    Webm,
329	}
330	
331	impl Container {
332	    pub(crate) fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
333	        match self {
334	            Container::Mov => "mov",
335	            Container::Mp4 => "mp4",
336	            Container::M4a => "m4a",
337	            Container::Wav => "wav",
338	            Container::Aiff => "aiff",
339	            Container::Gif => "gif",
340	            Container::Apng => "apng",
341	            Container::Webm => "webm",
342	        }
343	    }
344	
345	    /// The output file's UTI. On the AVFoundation path Swift passes this
346	    /// straight to `outputFileType`, whose raw values ARE UTIs; on the
347	    /// ImageIO path it is the destination type
348	    /// `CGImageDestinationCreateWithURL` takes. Either way it is what the
349	    /// save panel's content type and file extension are derived from, which
350	    /// is why the two image formats name a real UTI here rather than
351	    /// nothing — an export that could not tell the panel it writes a `.gif`
352	    /// would be worse off than one whose type string a session would
353	    /// reject, and a session is never built for them.
354	    ///
355	    /// An APNG is written to an ordinary PNG destination — the animation
356	    /// lives in `acTL`/`fcTL` chunks inside a file that is still a PNG — so
357	    /// its type identifier is PNG's, not one of its own.
358	    ///
359	    /// The two LPCM rows' identifiers are exactly `AVFileType.wav` and
360	    /// `AVFileType.aiff`'s raw values, which is what lets
361	    /// `Exporter.fileType(for:)` resolve them from this string alone
362	    /// rather than growing a container list of its own.
363	    pub(crate) fn file_type(self) -> &'static str {
364	        match self {
365	            Container::Mov => "com.apple.quicktime-movie",
366	            Container::Mp4 => "public.mpeg-4",
367	            Container::M4a => "com.apple.m4a-audio",
368	            Container::Wav => "com.microsoft.waveform-audio",
369	            Container::Aiff => "public.aiff-audio",
370	            Container::Gif => "com.compuserve.gif",
371	            Container::Apng => "public.png",
372	            Container::Webm => "org.webmproject.webm",
373	        }
374	    }
375	
376	    /// Whether `shouldOptimizeForNetworkUse` defaults on. MP4 and M4A are
377	    /// the delivery containers people upload, and a leading `moov` atom
378	    /// lets a player start before the file is fully fetched. A ProRes MOV
379	    /// is an editing master handed to another application, where the
380	    /// rewrite pass buys nothing. An HEVC-with-alpha MOV is a delivery file
381	    /// too, and its default stays off all the same: that was the owner's
382	    /// choice for the row (spec §11 G-33), and the override turns it on. GIF
383	    /// and APNG have no `moov` atom and nothing to move: a viewer already
384	    /// starts on the first frame, and
385	    /// neither do WAV and AIFF — a RIFF or an IFF file is a header
386	    /// followed by samples, with no index to relocate, so the flag would
387	    /// be a request the writer has nothing to do about. A WebM's index (its
388	    /// SeekHead) is already at the front, so the flag is off and inert there
389	    /// too (spec §11 CX-15 (1)).
390	    pub(crate) fn optimizes_for_network(self) -> bool {
391	        matches!(self, Container::Mp4 | Container::M4a)
392	    }
393	
394	    /// Whether the container can hold sound. Every movie container can,
395	    /// and M4A, WAV and AIFF are nothing else; GIF and APNG are picture
396	    /// formats with no audio track in the file format at all, so
397	    /// `audio: false` for those is a fact about the container rather than
398	    /// a decision about the project.
399	    pub(crate) fn carries_audio(self) -> bool {
400	        !matches!(self, Container::Gif | Container::Apng)
401	    }
402	}
403	//! The output sizes the export sheet offers for one document and one
404	//! format — `rc_export_sizes` (spec §7.8) — and the one rule for what a
405	//! size MEANS on an image format, which `export_settings` applies too.
406	//!
407	//! A preset is an encoding and carries no size (`export.rs`), so the size
408	//! is a second choice, and this module is the list that choice is made
409	//! from: the format's cap if it has one, the document's own size, and the
410	//! standard sizes fitted to the document's aspect. The FIRST row is the
411	//! default — the rule every list the export sheet is built from follows —
412	//! which is the document's size for a movie format and the cap for an
413	//! image format, because an image format's cap is the point of the row
414	//! and not a ceiling that only applies from above.
415	//!
416	//! **The number is the short edge.** A standard size is named by one
417	//! number, and the number people use is the short one: "1080p ultrawide"
418	//! is 2560 × 1080 and "1080p vertical" is 1080 × 1920, and both are 1080p
419	//! to everyone who says it. Naming by the long edge would call the
420	//! ultrawide 2560p and the vertical 1920p, which nobody does. So a row
421	//! keeps its short edge exactly and the long edge follows the document:
422	//! L = S × long / short of the document, on whichever axis the document is
423	//! longer along, and S × S for a square.
424	//!
425	//! **The long edge is rounded to even.** 4:2:0 chroma puts one colour
426	//! sample under each 2 × 2 block of luma, so H.264 and HEVC want even
427	//! dimensions, and `ExporterWriter.evenDimension` rounds an odd one down
428	//! before writing. Rounding here — to the nearest even integer, a tie
429	//! going up — means the size the popup shows is the size the file has;
430	//! leaving it to the writer would change the size behind the sheet's
431	//! back.
432	//!
433	//! **The even rule (spec §11 G-33).** The same is true of the document row
434	//! and of any size asked for, so on every row that needs even dimensions
435	//! (`Preset::even_sized`: every row AVFoundation writes but ProRes 4444)
436	//! the size is resolved HERE, by [`even_size`]: the document row's numbers
437	//! in this list, and in `export_settings` whatever was asked. An odd edge
438	//! is one pixel SMALLER. Down, because that is the size the writer already
439	//! wrote, so the report moves to the file and no file changes size;
440	//! because rounding up would hand the encoder a frame larger than the
441	//! picture on that axis; and because every listed row is then its own
442	//! fixed point, as an image format's is. The row is named "Document
443	//! (even)" when its numbers are not the canvas's, which is the whole of
444	//! how the popup says why. The argument this replaces was that a "Document
445	//! size" that was not the document's size would be a lie; the lie was the
446	//! row that said 321 × 181 over a file of 320 × 180. ProRes 4444 and the
447	//! two image formats keep an odd edge, and their row is "Document size",
448	//! the canvas as it is.
449	//!
450	//! **An image format's numbers are the file's.** A GIF or an APNG is
451	//! written frame by frame with the picture FITTED inside the size — aspect
452	//! kept, never upscaled — where a movie is letterboxed to exactly the frame
453	//! asked for (`ExporterImageSequence`, spec §7.8): padding costs bytes in
454	//! every frame for pixels that carry nothing, and a bigger frame carries no
455	//! more detail. So on those two formats every row here, and every size
456	//! `export_settings` resolves — the cap, a standard row, a custom size — is
457	//! the canvas fitted inside that box ([`fit_within`]), so that the popup,
458	//! the sheet's readout and the `export` tool all report the numbers the
459	//! file will have: a vertical 1080 × 1920 timeline's "GIF default" is
460	//! 152 × 270, not 480 × 270. The fit is decided here, once; the writer
461	//! draws each frame at exactly this size and does not fit a second time.
462	//! It is also its own fixed point — a fitted size fed back as the box
463	//! fits to itself — because that is exactly what happens: the sheet and
464	//! the tool send a listed row's numbers back through `export_settings` as
465	//! `width` and `height`, and a fit that could move a derived edge by a
466	//! pixel on the second pass would show one size and write another.
467	//!
468	//! **Rows may repeat.** A 1920 × 1080 document's 1080p row IS the document
469	//! row, and on a 1080 × 1920 document every image-format row from 1080p up
470	//! is the document again. They are listed anyway, because an id is the
471	//! `export` tool's vocabulary and a request for `1080p` has to mean the
472	//! same thing on every document — refusing it exactly where it is a no-op
473	//! would be the popup's tidiness leaking into an API. The sheet hides a
474	//! row whose numbers an earlier row already has, so a person never sees one
475	//! size under two names, and the row that shows is the one whose name says
476	//! more ("Document size" over "1080p"). Rows larger than the document are
477	//! offered for a movie — they were before, as the 4K preset — because a
478	//! 720p screen recording exported at 4K for a platform that picks its
479	//! bitrate by resolution is a real request.
480	
481	use serde_json::{Map, Value};
482	
483	use crate::export;
484	use crate::model::Project;
485	
486	/// The standard sizes, largest first, as (id, name, short edge). The id is
487	/// the `export` tool's vocabulary and the name is the popup's; they differ
488	/// only for 4K, which nobody calls 2160p out loud but which needs a
489	/// short-edge id to sit in the same vocabulary as the other three.
490	const STANDARD: [(&str, &str, u32); 4] = [
491	    ("2160p", "4K", 2160),
492	    ("1440p", "1440p", 1440),
493	    ("1080p", "1080p", 1080),
494	    ("720p", "720p", 720),
495	];
496	
497	/// One row of the list, before it is JSON.
498	struct Row {
499	    id: &'static str,
500	    name: String,
501	    width: u32,
502	    height: u32,
503	}
504	
505	impl Row {
506	    fn to_json(&self) -> Value {
507	        let mut out = Map::new();
508	        out.insert("id".to_string(), Value::from(self.id));
509	        out.insert("name".to_string(), Value::from(self.name.as_str()));
510	        out.insert("width".to_string(), Value::from(self.width));
511	        out.insert("height".to_string(), Value::from(self.height));
512	        Value::Object(out)
513	    }
514	}
515	
516	impl Project {
517	    /// The sizes the export sheet offers for `preset_id` against this
518	    /// document, as the JSON array of `{id, name, width, height}` rows
519	    /// `rc_export_sizes` returns, in menu order — the first is the default.
520	    ///
521	    /// The rows:
522	    ///
523	    /// 1. `preset` — the format's cap, "GIF default" / "APNG default", for
524	    ///    the two rows of the table that carry one; nothing for the rest.
525	    /// 2. `document` — "Document size", the canvas as it is; on a row that
526	    ///    needs even dimensions the canvas evened ([`even_size`]), named
527	    ///    "Document (even)" when that is not the canvas's own size.
528	    /// 3. `2160p` ("4K"), `1440p`, `1080p`, `720p` — the short edge named,
529	    ///    the long edge fitted to the canvas and rounded to even.
530	    ///
531	    /// On an image format every row's numbers are the canvas fitted inside
532	    /// that row's box, never upscaled — the size the file will have. Rows
533	    /// may repeat an earlier row's numbers and are listed anyway (the
534	    /// module doc says why); the sheet hides the repeats.
535	    ///
536	    /// One list for every movie format, the audio-only row included: a
537	    /// width is reported for it the way `export_settings` reports one, and
538	    /// the sheet disables the control rather than this module keeping a
539	    /// second rule for one row. `Err` for an unknown preset, naming it —
540	    /// the same lookup and the same words as `export_settings`.
541	    pub fn export_sizes(&self, preset_id: &str) -> Result<Value, String> {
542	        let preset = export::preset(preset_id)?;
543	        let document = (self.canvas.width, self.canvas.height);
544	        let fits = preset.fits_inside_size();
545	        let sized = |(width, height): (u32, u32)| {
546	            if fits {
547	                fit_within(document, (width, height))
548	            } else {
549	                (width, height)
550	            }
551	        };
552	
553	        let mut rows: Vec<Row> = Vec::new();
554	        if let Some(cap) = preset.size {
555	            // The codec in capitals is the format's name as people write
556	            // it — GIF, APNG — for the two rows that carry a cap.
557	            let (width, height) = sized(cap);
558	            rows.push(Row {
559	                id: "preset",
560	                name: format!("{} default", preset.codec.to_uppercase()),
561	                width,
562	                height,
563	            });
564	        }
565	        // The id is `document` either way: the name is the popup's, and it
566	        // changes only when the numbers are not the canvas's.
567	        let listed = if preset.even_sized() {
568	            even_size(document)
569	        } else {
570	            document
571	        };
572	        let name = if listed == document {
573	            "Document size"
574	        } else {
575	            "Document (even)"
576	        };
577	        rows.push(Row {
578	            id: "document",
579	            name: name.to_string(),
580	            width: listed.0,
581	            height: listed.1,
582	        });
583	        for (id, name, short) in STANDARD {
584	            let (width, height) = sized(fitted(document, short));
585	            rows.push(Row {
586	                id,
587	                name: name.to_string(),
588	                width,
589	                height,
590	            });
591	        }
592	
593	        Ok(Value::Array(rows.iter().map(Row::to_json).collect()))
594	    }
595	}
596	
597	/// The size whose short edge is `short`, in the aspect of a `width` ×
598	/// `height` document: the long edge is `short` × the document's long edge
599	/// over its short one, rounded to the nearest even integer with a tie
600	/// going up, on the axis the document is longer along. A square document
601	/// gives `short` × `short`.
602	fn fitted((width, height): (u32, u32), short: u32) -> (u32, u32) {
603	    let doc_long = u64::from(width.max(height));
604	    // `validate` refuses a zero edge; the `max` keeps the division total
605	    // regardless, since no input may panic.
606	    let doc_short = u64::from(width.min(height)).max(1);
607	
608	    // The nearest even integer to short × doc_long / doc_short is twice
609	    // the nearest integer to half of it, and round(a / b) with a tie going
610	    // up is (2a + b) / 2b in integer division — here a = short × doc_long
611	    // and b = 2 × doc_short, so the whole thing is one division. u64
612	    // because a canvas need only be non-zero (`validate`), not inside
613	    // `set_canvas`'s 16..16384, so the product is not bounded by u32.
614	    let half = (u64::from(short) * doc_long + doc_short) / (2 * doc_short);
615	    // A canvas far outside those bounds can carry a ratio no u32 holds;
616	    // the row is then unusable, but a query must answer, and evenly.
617	    let long = u32::try_from(half * 2).unwrap_or(u32::MAX - 1);
618	
619	    if width >= height {
620	        (long, short)
621	    } else {
622	        (short, long)
623	    }
624	}
625	
626	/// A size as a row that needs even dimensions writes it (spec §11 G-33),
627	/// each edge on its own: below 2 it is 2, an odd edge is one SMALLER, and an
628	/// even edge is itself. The rule `export_settings` and
629	/// [`Project::export_sizes`] share, so the list and the resolver cannot
630	/// disagree about what an H.264 will measure; the module doc says why down.
631	/// It is `ExporterWriter.evenDimension`'s arithmetic, which stays as the
632	/// floor under any caller that did not come through here.
633	pub(crate) fn even_size((width, height): (u32, u32)) -> (u32, u32) {
634	    let even = |edge: u32| if edge < 2 { 2 } else { edge - edge % 2 };
635	    (even(width), even(height))
636	}
637	
638	/// A `width` × `height` canvas fitted inside a box: the canvas itself when
639	/// it already fits — never upscaled — and otherwise scaled down, aspect
640	/// kept, so that the edge which meets the box first takes the box's value
641	/// exactly and the other is the scaled value rounded UP to a whole pixel.
642	/// The rule an image format's size means (module doc), shared by
643	/// `export_settings` and [`Project::export_sizes`] so the two cannot
644	/// disagree about what a GIF will measure.
645	///
646	/// Up rather than to the nearest, so that the fit is its own fixed point.
647	/// Fitting the result again compares box × canvas products on the two
648	/// axes, and the derived edge — never below its exact value — keeps the
649	/// same axis limiting, whose derived edge is the same ceiling; rounded to
650	/// the nearest it can fall below the exact value, flip the limiting axis
651	/// on the second pass, and take a pixel off the other edge (a 3024 × 1964
652	/// recording's 1080p box, 1662 × 1080, came back 1662 × 1079 and then
653	/// 1661 × 1079). The ceiling never leaves the box: the limiting axis is
654	/// the one whose exact scaled value fits, and a whole number no smaller
655	/// than a value that fits inside a whole box edge fits too.
656	pub(crate) fn fit_within((width, height): (u32, u32), (box_w, box_h): (u32, u32)) -> (u32, u32) {
657	    if width <= box_w && height <= box_h {
658	        return (width, height);
659	    }
660	    let (w, h) = (u64::from(width).max(1), u64::from(height).max(1));
661	    let (bw, bh) = (u64::from(box_w).max(1), u64::from(box_h).max(1));
662	    // The width meets the box first when box_w / w ≤ box_h / h, which is
663	    // box_w × h ≤ box_h × w with no division to round.
664	    let (fw, fh) = if bw * h <= bh * w {
665	        (bw, ceil_div(h * bw, w))
666	    } else {
667	        (ceil_div(w * bh, h), bh)
668	    };
669	    let edge = |value: u64| u32::try_from(value).unwrap_or(u32::MAX).max(1);
670	    (edge(fw), edge(fh))
671	}

docs/guide/export.md:36:- **Readout:** `1920 × 1080 · 30 fps · 00:01:12:05` (size, frame rate, duration). For the audio-only formats it reads `Audio only · 00:01:12.200`. For GIF and APNG it adds the frame count: `· 360 frames, no audio`. For **AV1 (MP4)**, **AV1 (WebM)**, **VP9 (WebM)** and **VP9 with Alpha (WebM)** a second line estimates how long the export will take: `Estimated time: about 25 s` (in 5-second steps under a minute, then minutes, then hours and minutes). It follows the format, Speed, size and range, and it is only an estimate: the figures behind it are the median of three measured exports per format at 1080p and 4K, of real 4K camera footage on an idle Apple M2 Max, so a slower or busy Mac, or a heavy timeline, takes longer. The other formats show no estimate.
docs/guide/export.md:49:| AV1 (MP4) | `.mp4` | The smallest delivery file, encoded by the AV1 encoder built into Frame Job. 10-bit, and it can carry HDR. Slower to export than HEVC. See [Speed](#speed). |
docs/guide/export.md:51:| VP9 (WebM) | `.webm` | VP9 in a WebM file, with Opus sound: the web format every browser plays, encoded by the VP9 encoder built into Frame Job. 8-bit, or 10-bit when it carries HDR. Slower to export than HEVC and larger than AV1 for the same picture. |
docs/guide/export.md:52:| VP9 with Alpha (WebM) | `.webm` | VP9 (WebM) that keeps a transparent canvas, for a title or a lower third a web page plays over its own background in Chrome or Firefox. 8-bit, always the SDR picture. Safari's transparent movie is HEVC with Alpha. |
docs/guide/export.md:93:| **Smaller file** | The slowest AV1 export and the smallest file. On the same footage it took about 1.4 times Balanced's time (19.9 s against 14.0 s at 4K, 5.8 s against 4.2 s at 1080p) and wrote a file 12 % smaller at 4K, 5 % smaller at 1080p. |
docs/guide/export.md:95:AV1 and VP9 are encoded in software, so they take longer than the HEVC formats, which use the Mac's hardware encoder. The choice is remembered with the rest of the sheet and stored in presets.
docs/guide/export.md:117:- For **AV1** the rate is a soft cap. AV1 encodes at a constant quality chosen to match or beat HEVC at that rate, so it usually stays under the rate and simple footage comes out much smaller. Very detailed footage can go over: up to about 1.25 times the rate was measured. Its tier titles and footnote read `usually ≤ …`.
docs/guide/export.md:281:Only HEVC 10-bit, both AV1 formats, VP9 (WebM), ProRes 422 and ProRes 4444 can carry HDR (VP9 with Alpha (WebM) is always 8-bit and writes the SDR version). VP9 (WebM) is 10-bit (VP9 Profile 2) for HLG and HDR10, and 8-bit (Profile 0, which every player decodes) for the SDR version. On every other video format the row is greyed out on **SDR version**, which is what those formats write. What each choice contains, and how the SDR version is made, is in [HDR and colour](hdr-and-color.md#exporting-hdr).
docs/guide/export.md:289:- **VP9 with Alpha (WebM)** plays with its transparency in Chrome and Firefox, in a web page's `<video>`. Safari has not been confirmed to show it (see Limits). Only a player that decodes VP9 with the libvpx decoder shows the transparency; others, ffmpeg's default decoder among them, show the picture opaque.
docs/guide/export.md:290:- **HEVC with Alpha** is the transparent movie for Safari, QuickTime and Apple's apps.
docs/guide/export.md:356:- Whether Safari shows VP9 with Alpha (WebM)'s transparency has not been confirmed; use HEVC with Alpha for Safari.
docs/guide/export.md:359:- On an M1 or M2 Mac Frame Job cannot play or re-import its own AV1 file, MP4 or WebM; QuickTime cannot either. Those Macs have no AV1 decoder. A VP9 (WebM) file re-imports on any Apple silicon Mac.
docs/guide/export.md:360:- AV1's and VP9's file size is not known in advance: the file usually comes in well under the rate, but very detailed footage can go up to about 1.25 times over it with AV1 and about 1.15 times with VP9.
docs/guide/export.md:364:- The estimated time is the median of three measured exports per format and size, of real 4K camera footage on one idle Mac (an Apple M2 Max). On exports it was not fitted on, 30 seconds at 2560 × 1440, it came within 14 % of the real time; a slower Mac, a busy one or a heavier timeline takes longer.
docs/guide/cleanup-tools.md:148:- **Only what is heard.** Words come from every clip that plays speech from a media file, clips inside nests included. A clip that is muted, soloed out or turned down to nothing gives no words. A clip whose words can't be read (its audio switched off, played in reverse, its file missing) is listed with the reason instead.
